skill.name: orchestrating-parallel-agents
skill.description: Guides teams through splitting large coding work into GitHub issues, launching parallel AI agents with git worktrees, and merging results safely.
skill.summary: Coordinate parallel AI coding agents with issue prompts, git worktrees, staged waves, monitoring, and merge cleanup.
skill.author: 4eyedengineer

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown fences, inline code, or documented command examples rather than executable Ruby code. No prompt injection was found in SKILL.md. The main security concern is explicit guidance to pre-approve git add, commit, and push for non-interactive agents.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow settings.local.json permissions to exact worktree paths and branch names, and require confirmation before push operations.

remediation.issue: Non-interactive agents can publish incorrect changes
remediation.suggestion: Require manual diff review before commit and push, and keep branch protection on shared repositories.

remediation.issue: Parallel wave size is not bounded
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run guidance and a recommended maximum wave size before production use.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Git Command Pre-Approval
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to permit non-interactive agents to run git add, commit, and push through Claude settings. This can publish unintended repository changes if issue prompts or agent behavior are wrong.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 69-75 directly grant git mutation commands for --print mode, and lines 79-82 launch background agents. This is intentional workflow behavior, not a scanner artifact.

content.value_statement: Large features are hard to split across autonomous coding agents. This skill provides a worktree-based workflow for issue design, wave planning, monitoring, merging, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Breaks large implementation work into isolated GitHub issues for separate agents.
Organizes issue batches into waves based on file overlap and dependencies.
Shows how to configure Claude permissions for non-interactive worktree commands.
Provides shell examples for launching, monitoring, merging, and cleaning worktrees.
Gives conflict handling guidance for sequential PR merges and rebases.
limitations: It does not create issues, branches, or worktrees by itself.
It assumes Claude CLI, Git, and GitHub CLI are installed and authenticated.
It requires manual review of diffs, PRs, and merge conflicts.
It can increase repository risk if broad git permissions are approved.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Wave
use_cases.description: Split a feature into independent GitHub issues and run one agent per issue.

use_cases.title: Batch Small Fixes
use_cases.description: Group small changes into waves while keeping same-file edits sequential.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Integration Work
use_cases.description: Schedule dependent waves after agents finish implementation work and initial PRs land.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe First Wave
prompt_templates.prompt: Use orchestrating-parallel-agents to split this feature into three independent issues. Identify files, dependencies, and review steps before spawning agents.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Agent-Ready Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft issue bodies for a parallel agent wave. Include problem, solution, files to modify, implementation notes, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Monitor a Wave
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the commands and checklist for launching agents for issues 101, 102, and 103. Include monitoring, logs, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Dependent Waves
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-wave rollout for issues that share files. Show merge order, rebase checkpoints, and cleanup after PRs land.

output_examples.input: A dashboard rewrite touches services, routes, and UI components.
output_examples.output: A wave plan separates independent service work, delays shared route edits, and lists review checkpoints before merge.

output_examples.input: Two agents finished, and one failed before creating a PR.
output: Complete the git steps manually in that worktree.
Create the PR after reviewing the diff.

output_examples.input: Several PRs touch the same component file.
output_examples.output: A sequential merge order with rebase checkpoints after each landed PR.

best_practices: Keep each issue scoped to one to three files with clear acceptance criteria.
Review every diff and PR before merging or pushing.
Run same-file changes sequentially or assign them to one agent.
anti_patterns: Starting many agents against vague issues with no file guidance.
Pre-approving broad git permissions on a shared repository.
Merging parallel PRs without rebasing after earlier merges.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples for launching agents with Claude CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes, as planning guidance. Replace Claude-specific command examples with equivalent Codex workflows when needed.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub issues?
faq.answer: The workflow assumes issue numbers as prompts. You can adapt it to local task briefs.

faq.question: Is non-interactive mode safe?
faq.answer: It needs caution. Keep permissions narrow and review changes before pushing or merging.

faq.question: How many agents should I run?
faq.answer: Start with a small wave of independent tasks. Increase only after the review process works.

faq.question: What should I do when conflicts happen?
faq.answer: Merge shared-file PRs sequentially. Rebase each remaining branch after earlier merges land.
